About the model

Model v3.1 · schedule board Fri Sep 25 2:11 PM CT · history through 2026-09-25 · 58,524 maps fitted · 481 teams · 2,471 players · market fit on 4,710 priced series.

Teams: Power is the one number. The model's own price on the Elo scale: 1500 is the average listed team, every 100 points is about 14 percentage points of map win probability against that average. Market-taught power, team Elo, player Elo, plus-minus and Weng-Lin (behind More columns) are inputs or cross-checks, not second opinions.

Players: Perf is the one number. The box-score composite the map probability is built from (kills, deaths inverted, economy-adjusted damage, KAST, opening kills, multikills per round), each in standard deviations against an average tier-S player over a 100-map half-life. +1.0 is a top-30 player, +1.3 the top 3. Plus-minus (rounds per map above an average player, teammates and opponents controlled) is the team-results check; it cannot separate players who always play together.

Schedule: times Central. Fair = the board's price (50/50 outcome-taught and market-taught; the lower of the two lineup prices when the roster is flagged). Edge = fair minus the price you would pay, in points; eROI = that edge over the price. Kalshi ask figures are after the taker fee; bid+1 figures are for a resting bid one cent above the current bid (no maker fee, fills only if someone sells into it). BET marks a side that meets betting rules v1:

What do these columns mean?
One row per seriesboth teams stacked, the first team on top; every column reads across for both. Map 1 / map 2 markets are inside the series: tap the row. Tap the teams to open the match in the Matchup tab (a team's card is a tap on its name there).
Startlisted start, Central time, with the tier; under it the countdown, LIVE, or the final score once the match is in the database, and the best-of
Model / Pinnacleeach team's chance in percent: the model's fair and Pinnacle's devigged line (the bold number is the favourite)
Kalshibid / ask in cents for each team (on a phone, the mid)
Edgethe model minus Kalshi's mid, in cents: green from +2, bold from +5; a dot = no reliable mid (no book, or one wider than 10c - map books often are)
Beton each team's line: BET = the bot's rules bet that team, with the markets in grey (series, map 1, map 2 - S / M1 / M2 on a phone); NO BET = they would, but the match is on the possible-fixing list; a dollar amount = what we already hold on that team in this series and its maps, bot and hand bets
Today S/A / Best bets / EverythingToday S/A = today's tier S and A series, finished ones included (the casual view); Best bets = series with a side the rules would bet, not started, on Kalshi; Everything = every series not started. The day and tier buttons and the checkboxes narrow any of them; the page remembers the last view.
Row detailevery market of the series for both teams: model, Pinnacle (with the first line the board saw), Kalshi, Edge, Bid+1 = the expected ROI of a bid a cent above the best bid (the bot's maker test), Take = the ROI of taking the ask after Kalshi's fee, Max bid, the rules in words, lineups and flags; Explore this matchup opens it in the Matchup tab
Red rows / POSSIBLE FIXINGa team on the possible-match-fixing list plays (config/betting.json exclude_teams): the match stays on the schedule, the bot places no bets on it, and its results are tracked apart

What do these columns mean?
Startthe series' listed start; rows in start order by default
Bet onthe team backed; YES on its market and NO on the opponent's are one bet
Costdollars at risk (both legs), tinted by size
Avgcost-weighted average price in cents
Fairthe board's price when the bid was placed
Edge / eROIfair minus the average price, and that over the price; green tints at 3/5/8 points and 10/15/20%
Result / P&Lsettled by Kalshi; open bets show a dash and count as open in the tiles
Todayonly matches starting today (Central); combines normally with Hide completed - both ticked = today's open bets, Today alone = all of today's
More infofill times, contracts, Kalshi's close (last hour before the start), CLV = close minus the average price, fill count, bot or manual
CLV *the reading is excluded from the tiles above - the close matched our own resting price too closely to trust, the bet was a manual live/in-play order, or the match is a known early-start case
Tilesopen stake and what it would win, settled count with the W-L, settled P&L, ROI on settled stake, dollar-weighted CLV and how often the close beat the entry
Flaggedmatches of excluded teams (config/betting.json) and the known early-start incident: listed in the table, left out of the tiles, the tier table and the audit unless Count flagged is ticked

Audit

Bot fills only, flagged matches out. Realized ROI on this few matches is mostly luck; the closing-line and the quoted-versus-filled tables are the ones to watch.
What do these columns mean?
ROI and its errorprofit over stake on settled fills; the error resamples whole matches, because a match's series and map bets win and lose together
CLVKalshi's price just before the start minus the price we paid, dollar-weighted, in cents; positive = the market moved our way after we bought. Fills whose close is not a real benchmark are left out
Quoted vs filledevery bet the bot had an order on, split by how many dollars filled. If the model's chance holds up on the bets nobody sold us and collapses on the ones that filled in size, the loss comes from who sells to us, not from the ratings
zhow far the win rate sits from what the model said, in standard errors; beyond about 2 either way is hard to call luck
Hours to startwhen the fill happened relative to the listed start; early fills have beaten the close, large late fills have not

What do these columns mean?
Impactour own player rating (model 3.0, 2026-09-25): the rounds per map a player adds over an average one - his box score (kills, deaths, damage, economy-weighted damage, KAST, opening duels, trades, multi-kills, clutches, utility; adjusted for tier and opponent, weights learned from results) corrected by his teams' round margins, with experience for newcomers. Built only from raw match data, no third-party rating. It predicts results better than bo3.gg's rating, HLTV's formulas and Valve's rankings (research/50). Players are ranked by it.
Perfbox-score composite in standard deviations vs an average tier-S player, 100-map half-life
Δwk / Δmoperf change vs the snapshot closest to 7 / 30 days back (2026-09-22 / none yet)
+/- rdsplus-minus: rounds per map above an average player, teammates and opponents controlled
*not on a current roster (team = last team played for)
More columnswin coefficient, player Elo, Weng-Lin mean and sd, effective maps, career maps and every component

Click a match above, or pick two teams, to explore the matchup.
What do these columns mean?
Matchesthe day's series, one line each (map markets folded in): time and tier, the teams, the model's and Pinnacle's chances (first team first), BET when the bot's rules bet a side; a finished series shows its score. S/A keeps tier S and A only. Click a row to explore it.
Win chancefor the first team: the board's model fair, Pinnacle devigged (from = its opening line), Kalshi bid / ask and Edge (model minus Kalshi's mid, cents) for the series and each map market; for two teams not on the board, the model's map / Bo3 / Bo5 chance from their Power ratings
Mapspick maps 1-3 (or click a map in the list) to see the map and series chances move: each map's chance is the board's own map price (for a match not on the board, the Power map chance) shifted by the two teams' map Elo offsets (a model component), and 'any' uses the unshifted price, so with no maps set the series chance is the board's; when a team's listed roster differs from the five who played last, Last five / Roster five switches between the board's two prices (it starts on the one behind the first team's fair; each side's fair takes the lower, so in the list above the two can add up to less than 100, marked *); Picked maps move to the top of the list in play order (M1, M2, M3); click one again to take it out. Likely fills each team's most-picked map (not the other's top ban) and the likeliest decider. The list shows each team's win rate and maps played in the last 180 days, and tags each team's most-picked and most-banned map.
Elo, last 6 monthsteam Elo from map results at the end of every week - the model's own team Elo, replayed; the logos mark whose line is whose
Comparisonunder Win chance: Power, the last 10 series, maps won and maps won above the Elo expectation in the last 90 days, the five's impact ratings added up (the better number bold)
Lineupsthe current five: Maps = maps played for this team (everything our data holds, since June 2020; amber under 20 = new to the team), then the stats from left to right in order of how predictive they are, sorted by Impact: Impact (our own rating - rounds per map a player adds, from his opponent-adjusted box score and his teams' results; the model's main input since 3.0), Perf (our box-score composite in standard deviations; a typical tier S player is about +0.5), K/D, the bo3.gg rating (0-10; maps bo3.gg had not rated when we fetched them are left out), ADR and form (last 10 maps vs the 90-day average; ADR and form not on a phone).
Head to headat the bottom: the record in the last 12 months and the last five meetings (month/day/year) with map scores
